title: Probability space
summary: A probability space assigns normalized weight to measurable events.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared measure-theoretic probability context is fixed.

content.plain: A probability space assigns normalized weight to measurable events.
content.exact: A probability space (Ω,𝓕,P) has a sample space Ω, σ-algebra 𝓕, and countably additive measure P with P(Ω)=1.
content.example: A fair die can use six outcomes each with probability 1/6.
content.caveat: Probabilities depend on the event algebra and model; they are not properties of labels alone.
